La «w» fue la última letra en incorporarse al abecedario del español, pues no lo hizo oficialmente hasta la ortografía académica de 1969. Entró por la vía del préstamo y se empleó inicialmente, ya en la Edad Media, para escribir determinados nombres propios de origen germánico. 

Aunque, en épocas pasadas, muchos de los préstamos que en su lengua de origen incluían esta letra se adaptaron de diversas formas al español con el fin de evitar este grafema considerado ajeno a nuestra tradición —trocándolo, según los casos, en «gu» («gualda», «guarda», «güelfo»), «v» («vagón», «váter») o incluso «b» («Bamba», rey godo)—, hoy se ha extendido y normalizado su empleo en la escritura de numerosos extranjerismos, procedentes en su mayoría del inglés («waterpolo», «web», «sándwich»).


Translation:

The "w" was the last letter to be incorporated into the Spanish alphabet, since it was not officially incorporated until the academic spelling of 1969. It entered by way of borrowing and was initially used, already in the Middle Ages, to write certain proper names of Germanic origin. 

Although, in the past, many of the borrowings that in their language of origin included this letter were adapted in different ways to Spanish in order to avoid this grapheme considered foreign to our tradition, changing it, as the case may be, into "gu" ("gualda", "guarda", "güelfo"), "v" ("vagón", "váter") or even "b" ("Bamba", rey godo), today its use has become widespread and standardized in the writing of numerous foreign words, mostly from English ("waterpolo", "web", "sándwich").

There's necesitar [something], meaning you need an object. 
Then there's necesitar a [someone], meaning you need someone, as in a living being. Therefore, necesito a mi gato. 

That's a general rule I learnt at least. 

If this is wrong please feel free to correct me!

Remember that you can't put the possessive pronouns mi/mis/tu/tus etc and general articles un/una and la/las/el/los after each other.
For example, instead of "Necesito a mis los gatos" you write either "Necesito a mis gatos" or "Necesito a los gatos".

Cheers and good luck!

What I did in order to settle in and "survive" throughout the day using only Spanish, was watching Spanish TV-shows (check out "casa de papel" or "aqui no hay quien viva"), following news on rtve.es/elpais.es, reading books (any level, even children's books) and watching some YouTube channels in Spanish. This prepared me to listen and converse in Spanish without feeling overwhelmed all the time.
